findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an Acceptance Criterion for the failure path: e.g. 'when the container is not running, `pytest tests/live_jira_dc/` reports a test collection/setup error containing the phrase "harness not running" (or equivalent), not a raw `ConnectionRefusedError` traceback — verifiable by stopping the container and running pytest.'
evidence: 'failure path: with the instance down, the marked suite fails with a clear "harness not running" message from the readiness probe rather than a raw connection traceback'
No AC in the Acceptance Criteria section corresponds to this claim.
findings.finding: The 'failure path' behavior — that with the instance down the suite emits a clear 'harness not running' message rather than a raw connection traceback — is described as a completion-relevant quality claim in the Testing section but has no corresponding Acceptance Criterion, so there is no proving command that would verify it.
findings.location: Testing section, 'failure path' bullet; Acceptance Criteria section (absence of a failure-path AC)
scenarios: The readiness probe could emit a raw `ConnectionRefusedError` stack trace instead of the described message, and no AC would catch the regression.
An agent completing the story could mark all ACs green while the failure-path behavior is never exercised.
findings.suggested_fix: Add as AC-6: `[ ] with no container running, pytest tests/live_jira_dc/ exits with a setup error whose message matches 'harness not running' (or a project-defined sentinel string from the readiness probe), confirmed by `grep 'harness not running' <(pytest tests/live_jira_dc/ 2>&1); echo $?` returning 0.`

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State default readiness-probe parameters in the plan (e.g. 'poll every 10 s, up to 5 minutes total, then fail with "harness not running"') so the executor does not have to choose them.
evidence: 'a readiness probe that polls until the instance answers REST' — no interval, timeout, or retry count stated
Jira startup on Docker is known to take 2-5 minutes; without a stated upper bound the probe has no termination guarantee
findings.finding: The readiness probe's operational parameters — polling interval, maximum wait time, and retry count — are not specified, leaving an executing agent to choose values that may cause flaky CI (too short) or indefinitely blocked runs (no upper bound).
findings.location: Approach section, 'a readiness probe that polls until the instance answers REST'
scenarios: Agent chooses a 30-second timeout; Jira takes 3 minutes to start on a slow CI runner; all integration tests fail transiently.
Agent chooses no upper bound; a broken image causes CI to hang indefinitely.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Approach or Scope: 'The readiness probe polls `GET /rest/api/2/serverInfo` every 10 seconds for up to 300 seconds; if the instance has not answered by then it raises a `pytest.skip` / `pytest.exit` with message "harness not running: Jira DC did not become ready within 300 s".'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC (or extend AC[4]) that explicitly verifies `make jira-dc-up` exists in the Makefile and successfully starts the container (e.g., `make jira-dc-up && curl ... returns 200`).
evidence: Scope: 'Makefile — a `jira-dc-up` target only'

findings.finding: The `jira-dc-up` Makefile target is named as a Scope deliverable but no AC verifies it exists or is runnable; AC[4] only verifies the `test:` target is unchanged, which would pass even if the jira-dc-up target were never added.
findings.location: Scope section ('Makefile — a `jira-dc-up` target only') and Acceptance Criteria AC[4]
scenarios: An implementer omits the jira-dc-up Makefile target entirely; AC[4] still passes because the test: target is unchanged.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend AC[4] to read: '`git diff Makefile` shows (a) no change to the `test:` target and (b) a new `jira-dc-up` target that runs the docker-compose up / docker run command.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC that verifies the readiness probe emits a recognizable 'harness not running' (or equivalent) message when the container is absent, rather than a raw connection traceback.
evidence: Testing: 'failure path: with the instance down, the marked suite fails with a clear "harness not running" message from the readiness probe rather than a raw connection traceback'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an ADR (or a clearly-signposted design-doc section in AGENTS.md) capturing the 'live-oracle verified-fake' pattern established by J5→J6, so future adapter stories have a canonical reference for how their fakes must be validated.
evidence: 'The fake is still built (J6 uses it for fast unit tests); this story gives it something real to be verified against' — this is a cross-story architectural pattern, not a purely operational detail
The plan references ADR 0037 §3 (an existing ADR) for teardown behavior, implying the project uses ADRs for consequential design decisions
tests/live_jira_dc/README.md is scoped to 'the pinned image tag and version-drift limitation' — operational, not the rationale for choosing oracle-over-pure-fake or the verified-fake contract
findings.finding: The plan introduces an architectural decision — using a live Docker oracle to verify a stateful fake (the J5→J6 'verified fake oracle' pattern) — that will govern how the DC adapter's fake is validated in perpetuity, but no ADR or AGENTS.md entry is planned; only an operational README is specified.
findings.location: Approach section ('The fake is still built (J6 uses it for fast unit tests); this story gives it something real to be verified against') and Scope section (`tests/live_jira_dc/README.md`)
scenarios: A future contributor adding a third adapter sees no documented pattern for how its fake should be verified and re-invents (or skips) the oracle step
A reviewer for J6 cannot find a canonical reference explaining why J6's fake must be validated against J5's harness rather than standing alone
findings.suggested_fix: Create `docs/adr/NNNN-live-oracle-verified-fake.md` (or append to AGENTS.md under a 'Test Infrastructure Patterns' heading) recording: (1) decision — DC adapter fakes are verified against the pycontribs Jira image oracle, not against recorded fixtures alone; (2) rationale — fixtures encode our own assumptions, the oracle can falsify them; (3) consequences — each new external-service adapter that ships a fake must also ship or reuse a live-oracle harness story. Reference this ADR from `tests/live_jira_dc/README.md`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a maximum retry count and/or wall-clock timeout for the readiness probe (e.g., 120 s with 5 s intervals), after which it raises a `pytest.skip` or `pytest.fail` with the 'harness not running' message — both in the Approach section and as an explicit AC.
evidence: 'a readiness probe that polls until the instance answers REST' — no bound stated
Failure path AC says 'fails with a clear harness not running message' but does not say when (after how many retries or how many seconds) that message is emitted
findings.finding: The readiness probe is specified as 'polls until the instance answers REST' with no maximum retry count or wall-clock timeout. If the container fails to start healthily, the probe loops forever and hangs the CI job indefinitely rather than failing fast.
findings.location: Approach section: 'a readiness probe that polls until the instance answers REST'; Testing section: 'the readiness probe reports REST answering'
scenarios: Container OOM-killed or misconfigured and never becomes healthy: CI job hangs until the CI runner's global job timeout kills it, producing an opaque timeout rather than the intended clear message
Docker pull is slow on a cold cache and probe gives up before the instance is ready, causing a spurious failure
findings.suggested_fix: In conftest.py, implement the probe as `for attempt in range(24): try: requests.get(..., timeout=5); break; except ...: time.sleep(5) else: pytest.skip('Jira DC harness not reachable after 120 s — run `make jira-dc-up` first')`. Record the 120 s / 5 s parameters in the README.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a maximum iteration count and per-iteration sleep to the teardown 404-polling loop (e.g., 30 retries × 2 s = 60 s), raising a descriptive `AssertionError` ('issue {key} still exists after {n} retries post-delete') if the bound is exceeded.
evidence: 'polls each issue's direct REST endpoint (…) until it returns 404' — no bound stated
'each delete call's HTTP status was 2xx' — 2xx is necessary but not sufficient to guarantee eventual 404
findings.finding: The teardown polling loop ('polls each issue's direct REST endpoint until it returns 404') has no specified timeout or iteration cap. If a DELETE call returns 2xx but the resource is not actually removed (e.g., a soft-delete that never propagates), the loop never exits.
findings.location: Approach section: 'polls each issue's direct REST endpoint until it returns 404'; AC line 3: 'every created issue returns 404 from its direct issue endpoint'
scenarios: A Jira bug or workflow hook leaves the issue in a non-404 state post-delete: teardown loop spins indefinitely, hanging the test suite
Transient network error during teardown polling never resolves, producing an indefinite hang rather than a clear teardown-failure message

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Document the concurrency assumption (single concurrent run per host) in `tests/live_jira_dc/README.md`, OR specify an isolation mechanism such as a randomised container name/port and per-worker Jira project key prefix so that parallel CI runs do not collide.
evidence: Fixed container name `--name jira` in the `docker run` invocation — no uniqueness strategy mentioned
Fixed host port `2990:2990` — only one process can bind a given host port at a time
No mention of CI parallelism isolation (unique project per worker, randomised port, Docker network namespacing)
findings.finding: The plan fixes the container name as `--name jira` and binds port 2990 on the host. If two CI jobs run concurrently on the same host (common with parallel pipelines), the second `docker run` will fail with a name conflict or port conflict, producing an opaque Docker error rather than a clear harness message. The plan does not specify isolation strategy for concurrent use.
findings.location: Approach section: '`docker run -dit -p 2990:2990 --name jira pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1`'; Scope section: '`docker-compose.yml`'
scenarios: Two PRs trigger CI simultaneously on the same runner; second job's `docker run` exits with 'Conflict. The container name /jira is already in use'
pytest-xdist is used within a single job; multiple workers share the single Jira container and the same scratch project, causing test interference

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the fixture performs a 'delete project if it already exists' step before creation (idempotent setup), or uses a randomised project key per run, so that leftover state from a previous interrupted run does not break the next run.
evidence: No mention of pre-run cleanup of a pre-existing scratch project
No 'upsert' or 'delete-if-exists before create' logic described
Teardown is noted as the retirement path, but partial teardown failure is not handled
findings.finding: The plan specifies that the fixture 'provisions a scratch project and tears down everything it created' but does not address idempotency of setup: if a previous run's teardown failed (partial state), the next run's project-creation call may fail because the project key already exists, leaving the fixture unable to start and the error message potentially obscure.
findings.location: Approach section: 'a fixture that provisions a scratch project and tears down everything it created'
scenarios: CI job is cancelled mid-teardown; the scratch project and some issues remain; the next CI run fails immediately at fixture setup with a '400 Project key already exists' error
A flaky test causes teardown to skip; accumulated projects eventually exhaust Jira's project limit on the test instance
findings.suggested_fix: Use a randomised 5-character project key (e.g., `TEST` + uuid4().hex[:4].upper()) so each run is isolated by construction, making both the concurrency and idempotency issues moot simultaneously.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the Makefile line-number citation from `Makefile:154` to `Makefile:177` (the actual location of `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` in the `test:` target).

Makefile lines 177-178: `test:  ## Run the default test suite (excludes integration + external).` / `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q`
findings.finding: The plan cites `Makefile:154` as the location of `pytest -m "not integration and not external"`, but the `test:` target containing that expression is actually at line 177–178; line 154 is inside the `actionlint-bin` target (a `set -e;` shell line).

scenarios: A reader or automated tool verifying the cited line finds an unrelated shell command and cannot confirm the filter expression exists where claimed.
If the plan is used as documentation or referenced in a downstream ticket, the wrong line number misleads anyone navigating to verify the no-Makefile-change guarantee.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `jira-dc-up` to the `.PHONY` declaration at Makefile:30 alongside the other phony targets.
evidence: Makefile:30: `.PHONY: help install hooks worktree format lint typecheck config-check check test vendor-security-rules changelog actionlint-bin verify-mcp-pin`
`jira-dc-up` is absent from the .PHONY list
Plan only states 'a `jira-dc-up` target only' with no mention of .PHONY

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Change the marker on `tests/live_jira_dc/` tests from `integration` to `external` (plus a `REBAR_DC_JIRA_URL` / `REBAR_RUN_DC` env-var guard in the conftest `autouse` fixture) so CI's `-m integration` leg never picks them up without Docker — matching the codebase's established pattern for opt-in infrastructure tests in `tests/external/`.
evidence: Plan: 'Every test in the directory carries the existing `integration` marker — not a new custom marker'
`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:447`: `pytest -m integration` runs in CI without any Docker service defined for the DC harness
Existing pattern: `tests/external/` uses `external` marker + `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL` env var for exactly this 'opt-in infrastructure' scenario
Plan rationale for `integration` marker: 'because `make test` runs `pytest -m "not integration and not external"`' — this avoids `make test`, but not CI's explicit `-m integration` leg
findings.finding: The plan marks all `tests/live_jira_dc/` tests with the `integration` marker, but CI's integration tier runs `pytest -m integration` (`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:447`) without Docker available — so the DC harness tests will be collected and attempted, producing connection failures in that CI leg. The codebase's established pattern for 'tests requiring opt-in infrastructure' is the `external` marker plus the `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL` env-var guard (see `tests/external/` and `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml`), which CI already knows how to skip. Using the `integration` marker rather than the pre-existing `external` marker is a clearly-inferior choice on codebase-alignment and CI robustness grounds.
findings.location: Approach section ('Every test in the directory carries the existing `integration` marker'); Scope section; AC[4]
scenarios: CI runs `pytest -m integration` on a build agent without Docker: tests in `tests/live_jira_dc/` are collected, the readiness probe fires, fails to connect, and the integration CI leg goes red.
A developer runs `pytest -m integration` locally without the container up: same spurious failure, with no clear 'harness not running' message at the collection stage.
findings.suggested_fix: In `tests/live_jira_dc/conftest.py`, add a session-scoped autouse fixture that calls `pytest.skip('set REBAR_RUN_DC=1 and start the DC container to run this suite')` unless the env var is set. Mark all tests in the directory with `pytestmark = pytest.mark.external` (not `integration`). Update AC[4] to verify `pytest --collect-only -m 'not integration and not external'` still collects zero — which it already does, since `external` is already excluded.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC (and a corresponding test path in the Testing section) specifying that every live test in `tests/live_jira_dc/` sets `allow_insecure = true` explicitly and that the test asserts the cleartext-risk warning is emitted, satisfying the parent epic's step 7 requirement that J5 is 'the intended allow_insecure case'.
evidence: Parent step 7: 'The J5 harness is the intended allow_insecure case, not an exception to it. The Dockerized Jira serves plain http://localhost:2990/jira, so every live test against it sets allow_insecure = true explicitly and asserts the warning is emitted.'
Leaf AC list: five ACs covering readiness probe, smoke test + PAT auth, teardown 404 oracle, pytest marker gating, and README — none mention allow_insecure or the warning.
Leaf Testing section: five test paths listed (happy, auth, teardown oracle, gating oracle, failure path) — none mention allow_insecure or the warning assertion.
ABSENCE: no leaf text sets or asserts allow_insecure=true in any test scenario.
findings.finding: The leaf omits the allow_insecure=true + warning-assertion requirement that the parent epic explicitly assigns to J5's live tests. The parent (step 7, security posture) states: 'The J5 harness is the intended allow_insecure case, not an exception to it. The Dockerized Jira serves plain http://localhost:2990/jira, so every live test against it sets allow_insecure = true explicitly and asserts the warning is emitted.' None of the leaf's five ACs or its Testing section mentions setting allow_insecure=true or verifying that the warning fires, leaving this parent-mandated behavior uncovered by the leaf's acceptance criteria.
findings.location: Leaf: Testing section and Acceptance Criteria (all five ACs); Parent: epic e369-a449-4773-48fb, Approach step 7 ('The J5 harness is the intended allow_insecure case')
scenarios: An implementer reads only J5 and writes tests that connect to http://localhost:2990/jira without setting allow_insecure=true, leaving the validator's override branch untested and the parent's explicit requirement unmet.

The parent's operator-attested AC ('rebar reconciles bidirectionally against the Dockerized Jira SDK instance') implicitly depends on allow_insecure working correctly; if J5 never exercises it, the path is unverified at integration time.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sixth AC: '`allow_insecure = true` is set in every live-test fixture that connects to `http://localhost:2990/jira`, and the smoke test asserts the cleartext-risk warning is emitted at least once per session.' Also add a corresponding bullet to the Testing section's 'auth path' or as a new 'security-override path' entry.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Evaluate whether `ArtifactTracker` + `_bilateral_teardown` from `tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py` (ADR 0037) should be extracted into a shared test utility and reused in `tests/live_jira_dc/conftest.py`, rather than re-implementing equivalent teardown logic from scratch.
evidence: Plan: 'the teardown oracle is not "query the project and find it empty": it asserts each delete call's HTTP status and then polls each issue's direct REST endpoint until it returns 404'

ADR 0037 / tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py already implement ArtifactTracker (partial-setup aware), _bilateral_teardown (bounded backoff, finally-block, leaked-artifacts.log), and the identical anti-search-index discipline
Plan does not mention ArtifactTracker or _bilateral_teardown, nor discuss why a new teardown implementation is preferred over extracting the existing one
findings.finding: The plan builds its own teardown harness (HTTP-status assertion + `/rest/api/2/issue/{key}` polling loop) from scratch while the codebase already contains a mature, ADR-0037-aligned equivalent (`ArtifactTracker` + `_bilateral_teardown` with bounded-backoff, partial-setup awareness, and a loud leaked-artifact log) in `tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py`. The plan references ADR 0037 §3 only for the anti-search-index rule, never considering whether the existing harness machinery should be factored into a shared utility or reused directly.
findings.location: Approach §5 (teardown oracle) and Scope (`tests/live_jira_dc/conftest.py`)
scenarios: The new conftest.py re-implements teardown logic that diverges subtly from the existing pattern (e.g., no bounded retry backoff, no leaked-artifact log), leading to a weaker guarantee than ADR 0037 already provides and creating two maintenance surfaces for the same idiom.
A future story adds a third live harness and again reinvents the wheel, cementing three divergent teardown implementations instead of one canonical shared utility.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract `ArtifactTracker`, `_bilateral_teardown`, and `_retry` into `tests/lib/live_harness.py` (or similar), import them in both `test_reconcile_live_e2e.py` and `tests/live_jira_dc/conftest.py`, and note the reuse decision in the README.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify and verify the exact mechanism by which the `conftest.py` fixture mints a PAT on the 8.17.1 instance (e.g., `POST /rest/pat/latest/tokens` with Basic Auth, or a pre-seeded PAT in the image), and confirm the endpoint is reachable with the stock `admin/admin` credentials.
evidence: Plan: 'a Personal Access Token minted on the 8.17.1 instance authenticates a request via Authorization: Bearer'
Plan: 'proving the DC auth mode the transport will use is exercised, not assumed'
No mention of HOW the PAT is created inside the test (REST call, pre-baked fixture, image entrypoint flag)
pycontribs/jira-test-image is designed for Basic Auth integration testing; PAT provisioning via its REST API on startup is not documented in the plan or cited from the image's own README
findings.finding: The 'auth path' test (AC line 2, Testing §2) requires minting a Personal Access Token programmatically on the running 8.17.1 instance, but the plan never specifies the mechanism — whether via the Jira REST PAT API (`POST /rest/pat/latest/tokens`), the admin UI, or pre-seeded credentials in the image. Whether the `pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1` container exposes the PAT REST endpoint and whether it is accessible with the stock `admin/admin` credentials without additional setup is an unverified capability assertion load-bearing to AC[2].
findings.location: Testing §2 (auth path) and AC line 2
scenarios: The PAT REST endpoint requires a Jira admin session cookie rather than Basic Auth, making it impossible to mint a PAT in a one-shot conftest fixture without a prior login flow — the smoke test silently falls back to Basic Auth and the AC claim is not actually exercised.

The image's servlet filter rejects /rest/pat/latest/tokens at 8.17.1 due to a configuration difference from production, and the workaround (e.g., using the legacy token endpoint or a seeded DB) is non-trivial.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the `jira-dc-up` Makefile target (and/or the compose file) is idempotent — e.g., it stops and removes any pre-existing `jira` container before starting, or uses `docker compose up --force-recreate`, so repeated/retried invocations always produce a clean, running harness.
evidence: Plan specifies `docker run -dit -p 2990:2990 --name jira pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1` with no prior `docker rm -f jira || true` guard
Scope names a `jira-dc-up` target but gives no idempotency contract for it
No mention of handling drift (e.g., container in Exited state from a failed prior run)
findings.finding: The `docker run --name jira` command (and implicitly the `jira-dc-up` Makefile target) is not idempotent: if a container named `jira` already exists (stopped or running from a prior session), the command fails with a name-collision error rather than producing a usable harness. The plan does not specify how the target handles pre-existing containers.
findings.location: Approach section / `docker run -dit -p 2990:2990 --name jira pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1`; Scope section / `Makefile — a jira-dc-up target only`
scenarios: Developer runs `make jira-dc-up` a second time after a failed test; Docker errors 'The container name /jira is already in use'
CI retries a job without a clean workspace teardown step; the harness fails to start and the root cause is obscured
findings.suggested_fix: In the `jira-dc-up` target, prepend `docker rm -f jira 2>/dev/null || true` before the `docker run` call, or switch to `docker compose up -d --force-recreate` so the compose file itself is the idempotency unit.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Lock the Docker port binding to loopback (`-p 127.0.0.1:2990:2990` in the `docker run` command and in `docker-compose.yml`) OR add an explicit, justified rationale explaining why network-wide exposure on CI hosts is acceptable (e.g., all CI runners are isolated single-tenant VMs with no external network access).
evidence: Plan states `-p 2990:2990` without a `127.0.0.1:` prefix
Docker default for `-p HOST:CONTAINER` binds to 0.0.0.0 (all interfaces), not loopback
Admin credentials are `admin`/`admin` — trivially guessable if the port is network-reachable
Plan provides no rationale for why network-wide exposure on CI hosts is acceptable (e.g., 'CI runners are isolated single-tenant VMs')
findings.finding: The plan binds the Jira service on `-p 2990:2990`, which Docker maps to `0.0.0.0:2990` (all interfaces) by default, not `127.0.0.1:2990`. On shared CI runners, cloud VMs with public IPs, or developer machines on untrusted networks, this makes the Jira admin console and REST API reachable beyond loopback. The plan refers to `http://localhost:2990/jira` as if loopback-only, but does not lock the binding or provide an explicit justification for the broader exposure.
findings.location: Approach section / `docker run -dit -p 2990:2990 --name jira pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1`; AC line 1 / `http://localhost:2990/jira`
scenarios: CI runner is a shared cloud VM with a public IP; Jira admin UI becomes accessible from the internet for the duration of the job

findings.finding: The Docker port-binding expression `-p 2990:2990` (and its docker-compose.yml equivalent) binds to all interfaces (`0.0.0.0:2990`) by default, not to loopback only. The plan does not declare the intended access posture of this port. On a shared CI runner or a developer machine on a LAN, this exposes the Jira instance — and its admin credentials transmitted over plain HTTP — to other actors on the same network segment. The plan is silent on whether loopback-only binding is required, which is itself the T5c gap (undeclared access posture on a boundary-crossing surface).
findings.location: Approach section (`docker run -dit -p 2990:2990 ...`) and Scope section (`tests/live_jira_dc/docker-compose.yml`)
scenarios: A co-tenant job on a shared GitHub Actions self-hosted runner or Jenkins agent reaches `http://<runner-ip>:2990/jira` and authenticates with the well-known `admin`/`admin` credentials, gaining full admin access to the live Jira instance during the test run
A developer on a shared office LAN inadvertently exposes the instance; PAT tokens and admin session tokens travel in cleartext over the LAN
findings.suggested_fix: In `docker-compose.yml`, change the port mapping from `- "2990:2990"` to `- "127.0.0.1:2990:2990"` to restrict the binding to loopback. Apply the same change to any `docker run` example in the README. Add a one-line comment in the compose file: `# loopback-only: harness uses plain HTTP and well-known credentials`.
